The 2024 disclosures D068, D069, and D070 collectively cover this same specific topic: D068 reports the 2024 revenue and the primary driver (higher market levels/AUM); D069 details the factors influencing revenues (AUM mix, client preferences, net flows in specific classes); and D070 provides the forward-looking statement on the impact of these conditions. These three 2024 sentences/disclosures form the complete counterpart set for the 2023 disclosure.

comparisons.peer_summary: Merrill Wealth Management revenue of $19.1 billion increased nine percent, primarily driven by higher asset management fees due to higher average equity market valuations and positive AUM flows, as well as higher brokerage fees due to increased transactional volume.
comparisons.comparison: Both MS and BAC attribute increases in their respective wealth/asset management revenues to higher average assets under management driven by elevated equity market valuations. MS reported an 8% increase in asset management fees to $5,627 million, explicitly stating it was 'primarily driven by higher average AUM on higher market levels.' Similarly, BAC’s Merrill Wealth Management revenue grew 9% to $19.1 billion, driven by 'higher asset management fees due to the impact of higher average equity market valuations.' While both cite market levels as a primary driver, BAC also highlights positive AUM flows and increased transactional volume as additional contributors, whereas MS focuses on the AUM/market level effect for the fee line item.
